description:
Graduate Route vs OPT vs Other Post-Study Work Visas (2027)

Direct answer box (first 50 words):

The UK Graduate Route gives 2 years (3 for PhD graduates) of unrestricted work rights with no job offer needed. US OPT gives 12 months, extendable to 36 for STEM degrees via the 24-month extension, but ties you to your field of study and requires employer reporting.

Why this comparison decides where you study

Post-study work rights are the single biggest difference between study destinations on paper — and often the deciding factor in practice. Three years of open work rights (UK PhD) is a different career proposition from one year of field-limited employment (US OPT). The table below is the 2027 snapshot; every one of these schemes is politically contested, so verify before you commit.

UK Graduate Route: the freedom option

You apply from inside the UK after completing your course, on a valid Student visa. There is no job offer, no salary threshold and no restriction on employer or role — you can freelance, job-hunt or stack temporary work. The doctoral advantage is real: 3 years vs 2 for taught graduates. For the application mechanics and the financial requirements of the visa that precedes it, see our UK student visa financial requirements guide and the step-by-step UK visa application guide.

The catch: the Graduate Route is a bridge, not a destination. To stay beyond it you must switch to a Skilled Worker visa, which does require a sponsoring employer and a salary threshold. The scheme's length and conditions are also under periodic government review — budget for the possibility of change.

US OPT: powerful but conditional

OPT (Optional Practical Training) lets F-1 graduates work in the US for 12 months in a job directly related to their field of study. STEM graduates on the 2025–27 designated-degree lists can apply for a 24-month extension, reaching 36 months total. Constraints that trip people up:

  • Employment must relate to your degree field; unemployment over 90 days (150 with the extension) can end your status
  • Your university's DSO must recommend it, and reporting duties continue throughout
  • Staying longer requires an H-1B — a lottery that roughly one in three applicants won in recent cycles

For PhD graduates in STEM, 36 months is generous, but it is field-locked and employer-policied in a way the Graduate Route is not.

Canada, Australia, Germany at a glance

  • Canada (PGWP): up to 3 years depending on programme length, any employer — but eligibility rules and field restrictions have shifted recently; check current criteria carefully. Its real pull is the PR pathway behind it (see our PR pathways comparison).
  • Australia (485): 2–3 years with any employer; regional study adds options. Recent changes have tightened age limits and English requirements.
  • Germany: no dedicated post-study work permit — instead, graduates get a residence permit to seek qualified work, and PhD graduates move quickly onto EU Blue Card terms. Combined with no tuition at public universities, the total package can beat Anglophone options — see studying in Germany for free.

Frequently asked questions

Is the Graduate Route the same as the old PSW visa? Functionally yes — the Graduate Route replaced the old Tier 1 (Post-Study Work) scheme in 2021 with the same core promise: open work rights for a fixed period. The PhD extension to 3 years is the doctoral advantage.

Can I apply for OPT and the Graduate Route? You cannot hold both simultaneously — they attach to study in different countries. The comparison is about choosing a destination, not stacking visas.

Does the Graduate Route count toward UK settlement? Years on the Graduate Route generally do not count toward the qualifying period for settlement, which typically starts when you switch to a work visa. Plan your timeline accordingly — see our PR pathways after study guide.

Which is better for PhD graduates, UK or US? The UK offers 3 years of fully open work rights and no lottery; the US offers deep-field salaries but a field-locked OPT and an H-1B lottery afterwards. If certainty matters most, the UK wins; if maximum earnings and you are STEM-listed, the US remains compelling.

Official source

All five schemes are under active political review and change frequently. Verify durations, fees and eligibility on gov.uk (Graduate Route), USCIS (OPT), IRCC (PGWP), Home Affairs Australia (485) and the German Auswärtiges Amt before making decisions.
